- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 3–4% after spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust — force a 1–2 day lagged correction downward.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate mean price; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” oscillations (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misreads momentum — apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
